2 ex-FBI officials charged with lying about involvement in investigation into Hunter Biden’s laptop
WASHINGTON (AP) — Two former FBI officials were charged Friday with lying to Congress about their involvement in investigating Hunter Biden’s laptop in the run-up to the 2020 presidential election, the latest in a series of splashy and politically charged actions the Justice Department has undertaken ahead of next month’s midterm contests.
Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former leaders of a since-disbanded task force set up to counter foreign election interference, appeared in federal court in Washington, where their lawyers pressed for a speedy hearing at which they could contest allegations that they lied to lawmakers by saying that they did not participate in FBI investigations of Biden.
The prosecution, a rare Department of Justice criminal case against a former employee, revisits a tangled and peculiar saga that roiled the final weeks of the 2020 race. It also comes amid a broader, backward-looking effort by FBI Director Kash Patel, who before taking over the nation’s premier law enforcement agency was a harsh critic of it, to scrutinize high-profile episodes from the bureau’s recent past that for years have animated President Donald Trump’s conservative base.” alt=”” />
Floris’ attorneys called her “a patriot” and said she has “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years.”
Two ex-FBI officials who specialized in foreign election interference have been charged with making false statements about Hunter Biden’s laptop. The AP’s Marcela Sanchez has more.
“Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts,” her attorneys said in a statement. “It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.”
Attorneys for Benavides accused the government of bringing “baseless criminal charges against him in a transparently political complaint.”
“This is another sad day for the Department of Justice,” his lawyers said in an emailed statement. “But now we are in court, and the truth will come out: Brad Benavides is a true patriot who devoted his career to protecting this country and its people. These charges are a disgrace.”
A criminal complaint comes just before the midterms
The case was filed 10 days before the Nov. 3 elections via criminal complaint, which means prosecutors have not yet presented the allegations to a grand jury for an indictment. The Justice Department has repeatedly struggled in high-profile cases to convince grand juries in the nation’s capital to return indictments.
During the former FBI employees’ court appearance, both defense attorneys and the judge noted the unusual move to charge the case through a criminal complaint, which is more often used by prosecutors when they have an urgent need to take people into custody because, for example, they present a danger or a risk of flight.
U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui remarked that it is “rare that we have charges this old coming in this nature.” Faruqui set a preliminary hearing for next Tuesday over the objections of prosecutors, who pushed for more time given what the judge described as the “sword of Damocles” hanging over the defendants’ head.
The laptop discovery created turmoil in 2020 election
The revelation of the laptop’s existence in October 2020 injected a thorny storyline in the race between Trump, the Republican incumbent, and Biden’s father, Joe Biden, Trump’s Democratic challenger, who went on to win the race.
The laptop were publicized by the New York Post, which said it had obtained from Trump ally Rudy Giuliani a hard drive of a computer dropped off by Hunter Biden at a Wilmington, Delaware, repair shop about a year earlier.
The criminal complaint aims to build on longstanding congressional Republican complaints about the FBI’s handling of the laptop, including allegations that the bureau was not forthcoming to the public that the materials on it — including emails that showed discussions of the younger Biden’s foreign business dealings — were authentic and not the product of Russian disinformation.” alt=”” />
The curious circumstances of the laptop’s discovery raised concerns among Democrats and former intelligence officials about the possibility of Russian involvement, particularly at a time when the Trump administration’s own intelligence community was Moscow that Russia was attempting to interfere on Trump’s behalf in the election and as Giuliani had traveled abroad looking for dirt on the Bidens. Dozens of former U.S. intelligence officials signed a letter saying that the laptop bore the “classic earmarks of an Russian information operation.”
But Trump’s then-director of national intelligence, John Ratcliffe, said in a letter to Congress that there was no proof foreign actors had anything to do with Hunter Biden’s laptop. The FBI under then-Director Chris Wray subsequently backed up that assessment.
Hunter Biden was charged with, and convicted of, gun and tax offenses during his father’s administration. Joe Biden pardoned him in his final weeks in office.” alt=”” />
The case shines a light on an FBI task force on foreign intelligence
The complaint alleges that in their capacity as leaders of the Foreign Influence Task Force, Floris and Benavides were deeply engaged in the investigations into Hunter Biden, and that Biden was a recurring subject at FITF meetings.
Yet, the complaint says, both downplayed their firsthand knowledge of the laptop or involvement in investigations during 2023 testimony to lawmakers who were doing their own Biden investigation.
It accuses Benavides of making a false statement by saying he learned through Wikipedia that the FBI was in possession of the laptop, and that Floris falsely claimed to have had no knowledge of Hunter Biden having been the subject of discussions at FITF.
“Lying to Congress by senior FBI officials strikes at the heart of our system. No one is above the law,” Patel said.
The case brings renewed attention to the work of the task force, which was established in the first Trump administration to police influence campaigns staged by Russia and other nations aimed at sowing discord, undermining democracy and spreading disinformation. The task force became a magnet of congressional Republican criticism during the Biden investigation and was disbanded in February 2025 by then-Attorney General Pam Bondi.” alt=”” />
The Justice Department has made other splashy moves
As FBI director, Patel has presided over widespread firings of agents who were involved in investigations of Trump or who are perceived as being against the Republican administration’s agenda.
He has also focused attention on years-old investigations like the Hunter Biden one that occurred before he became director and that have been the subject of grievances and complaints by Trump allies.
The Justice Department historically looks to avoid public and overt investigative acts in the direct lead-up to an election that involve candidates or that risk influencing a political outcome. But officials in the last two weeks have made a series of bold moves in cases with political undertones, including a search of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s house in an immigration fraud investigation and a corruption indictment unsealed Thursday against powerful Democratic Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas.” alt=”” />
Omar and Lucas are both Trump critics. Omar, who’s from Minnesota, has called the search of her Washington home an “attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.” Lucas has said she won’t be intimidated or bullied by the federal government in its case against her and “will not back down.”

sources.news_title: The Epistemology of Hunter Biden's "Laptop"
sources.text:
The first thing you should know about the complaint charging Nikki Floris and Brad Benavides with lying to Jim Jordan’s committee in 2023 is that they did not say the hard drive masquerading as a laptop that Rudy Giuliani rolled out in October 2020 was part of a Russian disinformation campaign.
They said they didn’t know.
On October 16, 2020, BENAVIDES wrote, and FLORIS approved, additions to the FBI Director’s talking points on the laptop for his call with Senator Mark Warner. The Office of Congressional Affairs’ draft stated: “The most I can say is that the FBI is in possession of an item that we lawfully seized.” BENAVIDES responded “This is good…you could add another if asked: Is the information we’re seeing in the press about a laptop containing emails associated with Hunter Biden part of a Russia disinformation effort? I can see from the perspective of anyone consuming this story that they could be concerned this is a Russia disinformation effort similar to what the FBI, ODNI, and other agencies have warned against; however, the FBI has not made that determination in this specific instance and as I stated before, I won’t comment on investigations or investigative actions.” He then wrote “Nikki, thoughts???” FLORIS responded “Looks good!”
So they can’t be the sources for any of a number of conspiracy theories that Jim Jordan, Kash Patel, and … everyone else claim to believe about 2020. They didn’t tell Politico, for example, that the Rudy Giuliani hard drive was Russian disinformation.
The second thing you should know is that the complaint substantiates materiality — an element of the charged offense — of what it claims are lies Floris and Benavides told House Judiciary Committee with what it euphemistically calls “information from a Congressional staffer.”
In connection with this investigation, the FBI has obtained information from a Congressional staffer who was present at the 2023 House Judiciary Committee interviews of BENAVIDES and FLORIS. The staffer confirmed that he or she viewed FLORIS’s statements concerning her involvement in and discussions of the Hunter Biden investigations as materially untrue. The staffer also confirmed that he or she viewed BENAVIDES’s statements on his awareness of and involvement in the Hunter Biden investigations as materially untrue. The staffer further stated that FLORIS’s and BENAVIDES’s answers influenced the Committee’s investigation significantly, including by thwarting investigative follow-up interviews and subpoenas. For example, had FLORIS answered the Committee’s questions concerning her awareness of discussions relating to Hunter Biden at the FITF truthfully, the Committee would have aggressively pursued all relevant information about those communications. Had BENAVIDES been truthful about his involvement in the Hunter Biden investigations, the Committee would have sought additional documents and testimony in furtherance of its investigation.
This “information” is horseshit. The investigation kept pumping out subpoenas and demands. More importantly, this pretends the goal was something other than killing the plea deal Hunter signed that summer, which the investigation achieved.
By treating this as “information” rather than “an interview,” the FBI may be attempting to avoid the necessity of jailing this Jordan staffer instead of Floris and Benavides. But I hope their attorneys insist on plopping that staffer on a stand sooner rather than later, because thus far, that staffer is making shit up to rationalize these charges, and doing so without any legal jeopardy himself.
Another critical detail to understand these charges: Everyone involved believes, as an article of faith, that the hard drive Rudy rolled out on October 2020, is the same thing as the laptop that John Paul Mac Isaac shared with the FBI in December 2019. Just as an example, after showing Benavides saying, on the day the NYPost story came out, “I would love to know if a copy [of the laptop] exists, and was it provided to anyone,” it then scolds that the next day, Benavides asks about the dissemination of the actual laptop.
The same day, BENAVIDES asked the Hunter Biden case team for specifics on the laptop that he already knew existed. BENAVIDES messaged FBI Employee 2 (one line is a separate conversation with another FBI employee redacted for clarity):
We are in the year of 2026, and we know the FBI did not, in 2020, forensically compare the Rudy Giuliani laptop with the one obtained directly from JPMI, and we also know that when introducing various devices into evidence at trial, the Cellebrite reports were substantially different. These are not hash matches. They are not the same device.
It’s not the same forensically. It did not have the same content. It is not the same technically.
And no one in 2020, or even in 2023, when Floris and Benavides allegedly lied, would have assumed the devices were the same! To do so would break every rule of forensic investigation taught at the FBI academy! It would be shoddy FBI work to do what this complaint demands these two FBI agents do.
But this is an article of faith. And like all true believers, one of the greatest law enforcement agencies in the world can no longer think of the Hunter Biden laptop and derivative hard drives as some hardware and some bytes that can be matched or not by forensic processes.
It is the laptop.
And so this criminal complaint treats “the laptop” as if the thing reported in the NY Post interview is as a matter of essence the same thing as the laptop JPMI had handed over a year earlier.
Which is to say, about half of the references to “the laptop” in this complaint are to the JPMI device (to make things worse, in one case the complaint claims that the FBI only got “the contents of Hunter Biden’s laptop,” which is false) and about half are references to the Rudy Giuliani hard drive, but the entire complaint treats them as if they are the same thing and — worse — as if Floris and Benavides would share what has become an object of faith 6 years later within hours of the first NYPost story.
Finally, you need to know that this complaint, rushed out 10 days before an election, is really poorly written. Perhaps most fatally, the complaint only belatedly explains the circumstances of the HJC testimony each gave at which they allegedly lied, and even then gives inconsistent explanations about the point of those hearings (which will undermine materiality claims). Which is how, 13 pages into the complaint, it introduces first the Chuck Grassley and Ron Johnson investigation (for which it relies on Benavides’ transcript) and then the defensive briefing about Andrii Telizhenko (for which it relies on the Floris transcript), and then having relied on both transcripts, introduces the interviews whence those transcripts were made.
23. In August 2019, Senator Charles Grassley and Senator Ron Johnson opened an investigation into potential conflicts of interest arising from the foreign business ventures of the family of then-Presidential candidate Joe Biden. Ex. 2 (Transcribed Interview of Bradley Benavides Before the H. Comm. on the Judiciary, 118th Cong. 69:6–12 (Sept. 28, 2023) (“Benavides Tr.”). Those alleged conflicts of interest related to, among other things, Hunter Biden’s role on the board of Burisma.
24. On August 6, 2020, FLORIS and BENAVIDES provided two separate defensive briefings to Senators Grassley and Johnson related to intelligence coordinated through the ODNI. Floris Tr. 23:13–24:1. During the briefings, FLORIS and BENAVIDES focused on potential Russian disinformation. Floris Tr. 28:20–29:6. When the House Judiciary Committee asked for specifics on the content of the defensive briefs during her transcribed interview, FLORIS testified that she could not get into specifics because the contents of the briefing were not FBI information—she directed the Committee to the ODNI. E.g., Floris Tr. 28:15–19, 29:13–15.
25. On August 25, 2022, Senators Grassley and Johnson sent a letter to FLORIS and BENAVIDES requesting their appearance to testify regarding FITF and the defensive briefings. The letter referenced previous attempts to obtain records and briefing appearances on August 12, 2020, May 3, 2021, July 25, 2022, and August 11, 2022. According to the Senators, they wanted to interview FLORIS and BENAVIDES “to explain the FBI’s interference in the senators’ Hunter Biden investigation.”
26. To investigate the FBI’s handling of the Hunter Biden investigations and related issues, the House Judiciary Committee interviewed FLORIS and BENAVIDES on July 19, 2023, and September 28, 2023, respectively. See Floris Tr. 3:2–4 (“Chairman Jordan has requested this interview as part of the committee’s oversight of the Federal Bureau of Investigation.”); Benavides Tr. 3:1–4 (interview requested “as part of the committee’s investigation of how and the extent to which the executive branch has coerced and colluded with companies and other intermediaries to censor speech”). The FBI has since obtained information from a staffer who was involved in and present for the interviews of FLORIS and BENAVIDES. [color coding my own]
There’s an effort afoot by John Solomon who — given the shoddiness of this complaint, may have drafted this — has been trying to resuscitate his Russian asset source, Telizhenko. My post on that is half drafted, but trust me, it is bullshit, like everything else Solomon does. Maybe they included him (and so the defensive briefing) originally but then realized Solomon’s fever dreams are not the stuff of criminal prosecutions? Maybe they want to include Telizhenko in an indictment?
The point is, though, that even on the most basic who, what, why, when, aspects of this complaint (they did get venue, the where, nailed on DC competently enough), it fails basic rules of clarity. Which, again, makes me wonder if Solomon drafted this, because he likes to do that too, leave out the Five Ws.
There are discrepancies in the testimony Benavides, especially, told HJC. But there’s no reason to believe it is a lie, unless you believe the Hunter Biden laptop is, as an article of faith.
According to Sarah Lynch, DOJ tried to stall a preliminary hearing, at which DOJ will need to prove they have a case.
“The alleged conduct happened years ago. The government has had the information about this for years,” said Ron Safer, an attorney for Benavides. He asked Zia Faruqui, the magistrate judge at Friday’s hearing in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, to immediately schedule a preliminary hearing “as soon as humanly possible” to review whether there was adequate probable cause that a crime was committed.
The politically charged case was also unsealed just about two weeks before the midterm election — a fact that may raise questions by DOJ veterans about the timing of a case involving testimony to Congress that occurred more than three years ago.
Faruqui said he thought the manner in which the case was charged seemed “strange” and he rejected a request by prosecutors to delay the preliminary hearing for two weeks or more.
He ordered the parties to return at 11 a.m. on Tuesday.
“This is the Sword of Damocles hanging over their heads,” he said. “This will follow them for the rest of their lives.”
But that’s not going to happen. We’ll be back here next Tuesday, a week before an election, to find out how much of this prosecution is really based on the Hunter Biden laptop as a matter of faith.
Update: NYT provides worthwhile background.
I was a bit suspicious when an FBI agent in Baltimore was mentioned in the affidavit. Wasn’t that where Barr set up a reception point for disinformation? With well-known hatchet-guy prosecutor Scott Brady. I’m likely remembering it incorrectly (Pittsburg?) but it rang a faint bell.

sources.news_title: Two Former FBI Officials Charged Over Hunter Biden Laptop Probe as Lawyers Condemn 'Nonsense' Case

Two Former FBI Officials Charged Over Hunter Biden Laptop Probe as Lawyers Condemn 'Nonsense' Case
Prosecutors allege Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides misled the House Judiciary Committee about their knowledge of FBI discussions before the 2020 election
Two former senior FBI officials have been charged with allegedly making false statements to Congress about investigations involving Hunter Biden. The case was announced on Friday, 23 October 2026, eleven days before the US midterm elections on 3 November.
Nikki Cole Floris, 46, and Bradley Benavides, 56, surrendered on arrest warrants in connection with the allegations. Floris's lawyers condemned the charges as 'nonsense' and questioned the timing of the prosecution.
Both officials previously held senior positions in the FBI's Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF). The now-disbanded unit was tasked with countering foreign interference in the 2020 presidential election.
Floris led the task force as deputy assistant director from mid-2019 through mid-2022. Benavides served as section chief from mid-2019 through the 2020 election.
According to the US Department of Justice, each defendant faces one count of making false statements in a matter within the jurisdiction of the legislative branch. The allegations concern interviews with the House Judiciary Committee in 2023. The department's announcement and accompanying court documents outline the prosecution's allegations. Neither defendant has been convicted of the offence.
What Prosecutors Allege About the Hunter Biden Laptop
The charges concern the officials' accounts of the FITF's involvement in FBI investigations involving Hunter Biden. Floris told congressional investigators that she had not participated in discussions about Hunter Biden while serving with the task force. Benavides said he learned the FBI possessed the laptop through a Wikipedia article in 2023.
Prosecutors allege that records, communications and witness accounts contradict those statements. The criminal complaint describes discussions between the task force and FBI investigative teams about the investigations.
According to the filing, the task force also hosted classified briefings involving agents and prosecutors. Floris and Benavides allegedly participated in those briefings and in discussions concerning the laptop before the 2020 election.
The complaint cites communications from October 2020 concerning the laptop and the FBI's response to media enquiries. Prosecutors say these records contradict the defendants' accounts to Congress.
The officials were warned during their congressional interviews that making false statements could be a crime, according to the Justice Department. The allegations must still be tested through the criminal process.
The Wikipedia detail is an unusual element of the case. However, the fact that Benavides reportedly referred to an online encyclopaedia does not, by itself, establish whether his testimony was criminally false. That question depends on the allegations and evidence presented in court.
US Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro criticised the alleged conduct in a statement announcing the charges. She said senior officials who lie to Congress undermine democratic institutions and that nobody should be above the law.
FBI Director Kash Patel also addressed the arrests publicly. In a statement reproduced by the Justice Department, he alleged that Floris had privately described herself as 'running a shadow government' during the 2020 election.
Patel further said the FBI had dismantled the CR-15 squad, which he accused of political weaponisation against opponents, including President Donald Trump. These assertions reflect Patel's stated position and should not be treated as independent findings in the criminal case.
Floris's Lawyers Challenge the Timing of the Charges
Floris's legal team responded forcefully to the allegations. In a statement, her lawyers described her as a patriot who had served as an FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years.
'It's no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now,' they said. Her lawyers argued that the allegations were based on politicians' claims rather than the facts and described the prosecution as an attempt to score political points.
The defence also said it looked forward to Floris's day in court. IBTimes UK had not identified a public statement from Benavides or his legal team at the time of writing.
The timing has added political significance to the case. The charges were announced eleven days before the 3 November midterm elections, while the dispute concerns events surrounding the 2020 presidential election.
The history also includes briefings involving Republican senators Chuck Grassley and Ron Johnson. According to the complaint, Floris and Benavides provided separate briefings to the senators in August 2020 concerning intelligence related to potential Russian disinformation.
The senators were investigating potential conflicts of interest involving the Biden family's foreign business dealings. The complaint's account of the briefings forms part of the background to the current allegations, rather than a judicial finding that either defendant committed a crime.
The laptop subsequently became a major subject of political debate and scrutiny of investigations involving Hunter Biden. Claims about the authenticity or significance of particular material attributed to the laptop require precise sourcing and should not be conflated with the charges against the two former officials.
The case began with a criminal complaint rather than a grand jury indictment. The defendants can challenge the allegations through the federal court process, and prosecutors must obtain an indictment to pursue the felony charges in the ordinary course unless indictment is waived.
The charges remain allegations, and both defendants are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. The proceedings will determine whether the evidence supports the accusations. Meanwhile, the timing of the prosecution and the defence's objections are likely to remain central to public discussion.

sources.news_title: Ex-FBI Officials Charged: Lied About Hunter Biden Laptop
sources.text:
The Justice Department charged two former FBI officials with lying to Congress about Hunter Biden laptop investigations, both surrendered Friday as the FBI director vows no tolerance for weaponization.
Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides, once senior leaders on the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force, turned themselves in Friday on arrest warrants after federal prosecutors accused them of false testimony about the bureau’s work on Hunter Biden matters.
Fox News reported the Justice Department charged the pair with lying to Congress about their involvement in FBI investigations into the former president’s son, including issues tied to his laptop. The task force they helped run has since been dissolved.
Floris served as deputy assistant director and functional head of the Foreign Influence Task Force. Benavides was the task force’s section chief. Both now face criminal charges over what they told lawmakers in 2023.
The Justice Department filed a statement of facts that points to sharp gaps between the officials’ sworn answers and bureau records.
Floris testified before the House Judiciary Committee in 2023. She denied any involvement in the investigation into Biden’s son. She answered no when asked whether there was “ever a discussion at the FITF about Hunter Biden” and whether she had “any involvement in the Hunter Biden investigation.”
Prosecutors say email logs show she discussed Hunter Biden with colleagues at the bureau anyway.
Benavides told lawmakers he learned “that there was an ongoing criminal investigation related to the laptop” by reading the Wikipedia page on the story. The Justice Department says emails show he was in contact with the team working the Hunter Biden investigation and that he met with that team before he sat down with lawmakers.
The Washington Examiner reported that Floris, 46, and Benavides, 56, surrendered Friday, and that FBI Director Kash Patel said documentary evidence, contemporaneous communications, and witness accounts contradict their July and September 2023 testimony that the task force was not involved in the FBI’s Hunter Biden investigations.
U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro framed the case as a direct hit on accountability inside federal law enforcement.
"Lying to Congress by anyone strikes at the heart of our democratic system, but when senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it’s time to bring the hammer of justice down on them,"
Pirro also said senior officials who choose deception over duty undermine the institutions they swore to uphold, and that the action makes clear no one is above the law.
"When senior officials entrusted with safeguarding our nation’s security choose deception over duty, they undermine the very institutions they swore to uphold. Today’s action makes clear that no one is above the law, and we will hold accountable all who obstruct the truth."
FBI Director Kash Patel tied the arrests to the 2020 election period and to the now-dissolved task force.
"This morning the FBI arrested two former FBI members of the now dissolved Foreign Influence Task Force, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, both of whom allegedly lied to Congress in 2023 on matters regarding investigations related to the 2020 election,"
Patel added a sharper charge about internal culture during that cycle.
"One of these individuals is on record privately claiming to be ‘running a shadow government’ during the 2020 election. As we’ve said repeatedly: weaponization will never be tolerated at this FBI."
Attorneys for both defendants rejected the charges and cast them as late-stage politics.
Lawyers for Floris called her a patriot with nearly two decades as an FBI intelligence officer and said the Justice Department accused her falsely on the say-so of politicians rather than facts.
"Nikki Floris is a patriot. She served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years. Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts. It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election,"
Counsel for Benavides stressed his record against terrorists and foreign agents and branded the complaint political.
"For 20 years Brad Benavides worked tirelessly to protect the public from terrorists and agents of foreign governments. He carried with distinction the heavy burden of thwarting terrorist plots to kill Americans and other innocents. Brad protected our democracy against those who would destroy it,"
His lawyer went further, calling the charges a disgrace and a transparently political complaint, while insisting the truth will come out in court.
The charges sit on top of a longer fight over how the FBI handled Hunter Biden’s laptop and foreign-influence claims before the 2020 election.
Republican Sens. Chuck Grassley and Ron Johnson previously accused Floris and Benavides of taking part in a 2020 FBI briefing about Russian disinformation. The senators said that briefing was meant to undercut their own probe into Hunter Biden’s foreign business dealings.
Claims that the laptop was Russian disinformation fueled intense controversy in the final stretch of that campaign. Years later, the FBI authenticated the laptop during Hunter Biden’s 2024 federal gun trial, when prosecutors introduced it as evidence.
That sequence matters. Officials told Congress one story in 2023. Prosecutors now say bureau emails and contacts tell another. The laptop itself moved from disputed object to courtroom exhibit. The Foreign Influence Task Force no longer exists.
What remains is a criminal case about whether two former task force leaders told the truth under oath about what they knew and what they did.
The core allegation is not exotic. Lawmakers asked whether the task force discussed Hunter Biden and whether these officials took part in the investigation. The answers came back as denials. The Justice Department says the paper trail does not match.
Floris’s no’s on FITF discussions and personal involvement sit against email traffic prosecutors describe as proof of those very talks. Benavides’s Wikipedia account sits against emails that place him in contact with the investigative team and in a meeting with that team before his session with lawmakers.
If those records hold up, the problem is straightforward: senior FBI figures gave Congress a clean story that internal communications appear to dirty up. If the defense is right, the government is stretching old disputes into criminal counts for political timing. A courtroom will have to sort that out.
Either way, the public now has something it lacked for years of laptop arguments and briefing fights: sworn testimony set against specific bureau emails, with arrest warrants already served.
When FBI leaders treat Congress like an audience to manage instead of a branch to answer, trust collapses. These charges put that habit on trial where it belongs.

sources.news_title: Two Ex-FBI Agents Are Arrested as the Hunter Biden Laptop Scandal Returns
sources.text:
The Hunter Biden laptop saga is back with a vengeance, with the Justice Department on Friday criminally charging two former high-ranking FBI agents with lying to Congress — settling a long-running score for Republicans who felt the pair had impeded their attempt to make the scandal a decisive issue in the 2020 election.
Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, announced that both former bureau officials surrendered Friday after arrest warrants were issued in a legal complaint filed Tuesday. The investigation was led out of the FBI’s Kansas field office.
The former agents ran the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force, which was created in 2017 under then-Director Christopher Wray in the aftermath of Russia’s attempts to influence the 2016 election by maligning Democratic presidential candidate Hillary Clinton. It was disbanded weeks after President Donald Trump returned to the White House last year, as part of his transformation of the FBI.
Nikki Floris, 46, was the task force’s assistant director, and Bradley Benavides, 56, was its section chief. After their tenure on that team, both were pulled into House Judiciary Committee Chair Jim Jordan’s yearslong crusade to probe the business activities of President Joe Biden’s son.
Trending
The inquiry dates back to an incident in which Hunter Biden left his laptop at a Wilmington, Delaware, computer repair shop in 2019, only to have it turned over to MAGA stalwart Rudy Giuliani. The former New York City mayor handed it to the FBI, and the saga eventually blew up into a scandal following a New York Post story in the closing weeks of the 2020 presidential election alleging improper political influence tied to Hunter Biden’s business interests in Ukraine.
Floris and Benavides “knew about and were actively involved in the FBI’s investigations of Hunter Biden” but repeatedly feigned ignorance when answering the Judiciary Committee’s questions during two interviews in 2023, according to a 27-page affidavit written by FBI Special Agent Byron Militello, a longtime investigator at the bureau in the Midwest.
The affidavit alleges that Floris was directly involved with the way the bureau fielded press inquiries following the Post’s story on Oct. 14, 2020, and even approved additions to
Wray’s talking points about the matter for a call with Sen. Mark Warner (D-Virginia). And it points to her conflicting answer in 2023 when the House Judiciary Committee asked how long the FBI had the laptop.
“I don’t know what laptop the article was referring to,” it quotes her as saying.
The affidavit also cites messages between Benavides and a person who appears to have been the assistant special agent in charge of the Baltimore field office, in which they discuss when exactly the laptop was seized and whether emails on it were shared with agents in New York. However, the affidavit says, Benavides told Jordan’s committee otherwise.
“I was made aware per the Wikipedia article that the FBI had taken possession of a
laptop circa December of 2019,” it quotes him saying in a transcript.
“Okay. You didn’t have that knowledge from your role in the FBI?” he was asked.
“Absolutely not,” he responded, according to the transcript.
Court records show that Floris is being represented by several lawyers including Margaret Donovan, a Connecticut attorney who is representing several FBI agents being targeted by the Trump administration. Benavides’ lawyer is Kimberly Paschall, who until last year was a senior attorney in the same D.C. office now prosecuting her client and has publicly signed on to a letter protesting what it calls the weaponization of the DOJ. Paschall did not respond to a request for comment.
Donovan and Washington Litigation Group lawyers Mary Dohrmann and Kyle Freeny put out a statement calling Floris “a patriot.”
“She served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years. Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts. Both surrendered to authorities and made their first appearance in a federal court in Washington. Their lawyers asked for a quick hearing so they could fight the charges.
This is a rare case. The Department of Justice has charged a former employee with a crime, and this does not happen often. It also comes as FBI Director Kash Patel looks into big events from the FBI’s recent past. Before he became FBI chief, Patel was a strong critic of the agency. These events have kept President Donald Trump’s conservative supporters upset for years.
Floris’ attorneys called her “a patriot” and said she has “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years.”

Both the defense lawyers and the judge pointed out that this was an unusual move. A criminal complaint is more often used when prosecutors urgently need to take people into custody, for example if they are a danger or may flee.

FBI Director Kash Patel on Friday outlined allegations against two former senior FBI officials charged with lying to Congress about their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden’s laptop, reviving a controversy that shaped the final weeks of the 2020 presidential election.
Nikki Cole Floris, 46, and Bradley Benavides, 56, surrendered to authorities on Friday after a criminal complaint accused each of making materially false statements to the House Judiciary Committee during interviews in 2023. Both face one count under federal law prohibiting knowingly and willfully making false statements in matters within the jurisdiction of the legislative branch.
The charges were filed less than two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections.
Patel said in a post on X Friday that the charges against the agents stemmed from an ongoing investigation into the since-dissolved FBI Foreign Influence Task Force (FITF).
"Floris led the FITF as a Deputy Assistant Director from mid-2019 through mid-2022. Benavides was the FITF Section Chief from mid-2019 through the 2020 election. Both testified that the FITF was not involved in the Hunter Biden investigations. Documentary evidence, contemporaneous communications, and witness accounts contradict their testimony," Patel wrote on X.
Patel also referred to an allegation that Floris privately described herself as “running a shadow government” during the 2020 election. "Lying to Congress by senior FBI officials strikes at the heart of our system. No one is above the law," he added.
“Witness accounts and contemporaneous documents from December 2019 through September 2021 show that Floris and Benavides knew about and were actively involved in the FBI’s investigations of Hunter Biden,” the legal complaint said, adding that both participated in classified briefings on the case.
During a July 2023 interview with the House Judiciary Committee, Floris denied involvement when asked whether she had participated in the Hunter Biden investigation, according to the complaint. Asked whether the Foreign Influence Task Force had discussed Biden, she responded, “No. At least not with me.”
Benavides, interviewed by the committee in September 2023, reportedly said he learned details about the laptop investigation from Wikipedia while preparing for the hearing.
The complaint cites a congressional staffer who attended both interviews and later told investigators that the officials’ testimony appeared “materially untrue.” It also describes an FBI employee’s account of discussing the laptop with Benavides and reviewing its contents.
“Floris testified that she had no involvement in the Hunter Biden investigations. In reality, she was in frequent communication with the case team for over a year,” the complaint alleged, adding that Benavides’ testimony followed a similar pattern.
The legal teams for both Floris and Benavides have pointed to the unusual timing of the charges, which have been filed several years after the alleged conduct, 11 days before the election.
"It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election," Floris' attorneys Margaret Donovan and Chris Mattei from Koskoff, Koskoff & Bieder and Mary Dohrmann and Kyle R. Freeny of Washington Litigation Group said in a joint statement on Friday.
Ron Safer, an attorney for Benavides, also noted the timing in court, telling the Friday hearing in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia that, "The alleged conduct happened years ago. The government has had the information about this for years."
He also urged the judge to reject prosecutors' request to delay the preliminary hearing by more than two weeks, which would push the date past the midterms. Instead, he called for the hearing, which determines if there is adequate probable cause that a crime was committed, to be held "as soon as humanly possible."
Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui, who was presiding at Friday's hearing, acknowledged that the manner in which the agents were charged was "strange," and rejected the prosecutors' request to delay. Instead, he ordered the parties to return at 11 a.m. on Tuesday.
"This is the Sword of Damocles hanging over their heads," he said. "This will follow them for the rest of their lives."
Meanwhile, Floris' legal team called the charges a "sad day for the DOJ."
“Nikki Floris is a patriot. She served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years. Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts," they said in a statement.
“The government’s reasons for charging Nikki are as transparent as they are unjust: to push a false narrative for a shot at political points. It’s another sad day for the DOJ, but we look forward to Nikki’s day in court.”
Newsweek has reached out to Safer and Floris' legal team for further comment.
Hunter Biden’s Laptop Scandal Explained
The controversy began after Hunter Biden, the son of then-presidential candidate Joe Biden, left a MacBook at a Delaware computer repair shop in 2019, according to the shop owner. The FBI obtained the computer’s contents that December as part of investigations involving potential tax and money-laundering offenses, according to the newly filed affidavit.
The laptop became a political flashpoint on October 14, 2020, when the New York Post published emails it said came from a copy of the hard drive provided by Rudy Giuliani, a lawyer for then-President Donald Trump.
The published material included correspondence about Hunter Biden’s business dealings in Ukraine and his position on the board of Burisma, a Ukrainian natural gas company. One email attributed to Burisma adviser Vadym Pozharskyi thanked Hunter Biden for an opportunity to meet his father, then vice president. The correspondence raised questions about potential overlaps between Hunter Biden’s business relationships and his father’s public responsibilities, but the email alone did not establish that Joe Biden took official action to benefit his son. Joe Biden denied involvement in his son’s business dealings.
The laptop and related digital evidence also drew attention for photographs, videos and messages documenting Hunter Biden’s drug use. During his 2024 federal gun trial, prosecutors presented messages and other evidence concerning crack cocaine to support allegations that Biden had lied about his drug use when purchasing a firearm in 2018. He was convicted by a jury of three felony firearm offenses in June 2024. He later pleaded guilty to three felony tax offenses and six misdemeanor tax offenses in a separate federal case.
In December 2024, President Joe Biden granted his son a full and unconditional pardon covering federal offenses committed or potentially committed between January 1, 2014, and December 1, 2024, including the gun and tax cases.
With the 2020 election approaching, Trump and his allies cited the emails as evidence of potential corruption, while some former intelligence officials warned that the circumstances surrounding their release bore hallmarks of a possible Russian influence operation. Subsequent examinations supported the authenticity of at least some laptop data, including emails, although questions about the chain of custody and the integrity of individual files remained relevant.
The Justice Department’s announcement on Friday alleges that Floris and Benavides discussed the laptop and the bureau’s response to reporting about it, despite later telling Congress that the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force was not involved in the Hunter Biden investigations.
“Lying to Congress by anyone strikes at the heart of our democratic system but when senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it’s time to bring the hammer of justice down on them,” said U.S. Attorney Pirro Friday.
“When senior officials entrusted with safeguarding our nation’s security choose deception over duty, they undermine the very institutions they swore to uphold. Today’s action makes clear that no one is above the law, and we will hold accountable all who obstruct the truth.”

Two former senior FBI officials are now facing federal charges over what prosecutors say they told Congress about the bureau’s Hunter Biden investigations.
Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides surrendered Friday on arrest warrants issued after a criminal complaint charged each of them with making false statements to Congress.
The two defendants once held leadership positions inside the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force, the unit created to defend the 2020 election from foreign interference.
Now federal prosecutors say both officials concealed how deeply that task force had been involved in matters connected to Hunter Biden.
U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced the arrests Friday morning:
This morning, two former senior FBI officials, Nikki Floris, 46, and Bradley Benavides, 56, surrendered on arrest warrants after being charged with lying to Congress about their roles on the Foreign Influence Task Force during the 2020 election. Floris and Benavides allegedly…
— US Attorney Pirro (@USAttyPirro) October 23, 2026
According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia, Floris, 46, of Alexandria, Virginia, led the Foreign Influence Task Force as a deputy assistant director from mid-2019 through mid-2022. The unit coordinated the bureau’s response to suspected foreign efforts to influence American elections.
Benavides, 56, of Aiken, South Carolina, served as the task force’s section chief from mid-2019 through the 2020 election. Prosecutors say both officials were involved in briefings and communications touching the Hunter Biden matters.
That timing is central to the case.
The Justice Department says the task force participated in several FBI investigations involving Hunter Biden before the 2020 election. In 2023, the House Judiciary Committee interviewed Floris and Benavides about that work and warned each of them that lying to Congress was a crime.
Prosecutors allege Floris told lawmakers she had not been involved in discussions about Hunter Biden while leading the task force.
Benavides allegedly testified that he learned the FBI possessed Hunter Biden’s laptop only after reading a Wikipedia article in 2023.
The criminal complaint tells a very different story.
According to prosecutors, documentary evidence, contemporaneous communications and witness accounts show Floris routinely discussed the bureau’s Hunter Biden investigations for more than a year. The government also alleges Benavides discussed the laptop with other FBI officials before the 2020 election.
The department says each defendant is charged with one count of making false statements in a matter within the jurisdiction of the legislative branch, an alleged violation of 18 U.S.C. § 1001(a)(2).
Its announcement emphasizes that the task force led the FBI’s efforts to protect the election from foreign malign influence while also participating in several Hunter Biden investigations.
That combination is why the 2023 testimony matters so much. Congress was not asking two peripheral employees what they had heard through office gossip.
Lawmakers were questioning the former leaders of the unit that prosecutors now say took part in the very matters they denied knowing about.
FBI Director Kash Patel said the arrests grew out of an ongoing investigation into the now-dissolved task force:
Two former senior FBI officials, Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides, were taken into custody today on charges of allegedly lying to Congress about their involvement in the FBI’s investigations into Hunter Biden.
The charges stem from an ongoing investigation into the…
— FBI Director Kash Patel (@FBIDirectorKash) October 23, 2026
Each defendant is charged with one count of making false statements in a matter within the jurisdiction of the legislative branch, an alleged violation of 18 U.S.C. § 1001(a)(2).
That statute makes the alleged lie—not the underlying Hunter Biden investigation—the immediate criminal issue before the court.
The complaint does not establish that either defendant manipulated the 2020 election, suppressed the laptop story or improperly influenced the underlying investigations. Prosecutors will have to prove the charged false statements with admissible evidence.
The charging papers do, however, revive one of the most bitter disputes from the final weeks of the 2020 campaign: what the FBI knew about Hunter Biden’s laptop, how the bureau treated the material and what senior officials later told congressional investigators.
The Associated Press reported that both defendants appeared in federal court in Washington after surrendering. Their attorneys pressed for a fast opportunity to challenge the government’s evidence.
The case arrived through a criminal complaint rather than a grand-jury indictment, a procedural choice that drew attention inside the courtroom because the alleged statements date back to 2023.
U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui set a preliminary hearing for Tuesday after the defense objected to a longer delay. At that hearing, prosecutors are expected to face an early test of whether the complaint establishes probable cause.
The judge reportedly described the unresolved accusation as a “sword of Damocles” hanging over the defendants and noted the rarity of old allegations arriving in this form. Prosecutors asked for more time, but the court chose a faster timetable, giving the defense an unusually quick chance to test the government’s theory.
Floris’ attorneys flatly deny the accusation.
They described her as a patriot who served in FBI intelligence for nearly two decades and accused the Justice Department of filing a politically motivated case shortly before the midterm election. Their response makes clear that the government should expect an aggressive fight over the evidence, the timing and the meaning of her congressional testimony.
CBS News reviewed the complaint and reported that it centers on the officials’ alleged awareness of and involvement in the Hunter Biden investigations. The filing cites witness accounts and records from 2019 through 2021 that prosecutors say contradict the defendants’ later testimony.
The complaint describes a counterintelligence operation called “Round River,” which allegedly collected derogatory informant reporting involving Hunter Biden so the material could be assessed for possible Russian disinformation. Prosecutors say task-force leaders participated in classified briefings for agents and prosecutors working on the Hunter Biden matters.
It also cites a congressional staff member who attended both interviews and later told investigators that the officials’ testimony appeared materially untrue. An FBI employee separately told investigators that he had spoken with Benavides about the laptop and discussed reviewing its contents.
One allegation is already drawing enormous political attention.
Patel said one of the former officials had privately claimed to be “running a shadow government” during the 2020 election. The Justice Department’s announcement did not fully explain the context of that statement, and the remark itself is not the false statement charged in the complaint.
House Judiciary Committee Republicans identified Floris in their reaction:
Nikki Floris admitted she was running a “shadow government.”
Today the real government caught her. pic.twitter.com/ExjzMeI6bk
— House Judiciary GOP 🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸 (@JudiciaryGOP) October 23, 2026
That line will dominate the political conversation.
But the courtroom battle will turn on something narrower and more concrete: the exact questions Congress asked, the exact answers Floris and Benavides gave, what they knew at the time and whether prosecutors can prove beyond a reasonable doubt that either answer was knowingly false.
The documents and witness testimony described by the government may be substantial. They have not yet been tested through cross-examination.
Both defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.
The next major moment comes Tuesday, when the Justice Department will have to begin moving this case from a dramatic announcement toward evidence that can survive in court.

DOJ says former FBI officials lied to Congress about Hunter Biden probe
Case centers on what the pair told the House Judiciary Committee in 2023
Two former FBI officials have been charged with lying to Congress over the agency’s investigation of Hunter Biden, the Trump administration announced Friday, unveiling its latest high-profile case in the weeks ahead of the midterm elections.
The complaint alleges that Nicole Floris and Bradley Benavides lied to Congress on two occasions in 2023. The pair worked for the FBI’s now-shuttered Foreign Influence Task Force and made initial court appearances Friday in Washington, D.C.
The charge for each could carry up to five years in prison, but a grand jury would need to approve an indictment.
The case centers on what the pair told the House Judiciary Committee about the FBI’s probes into then-candidate Joe Biden’s second son in the lead-up to the 2020 presidential race, including how much they knew about an infamous laptop that was left at a Delaware computer repair shop, according to a statement of facts filed along with the case.
U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro trumpeted the charges Friday.
“When senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it’s time to bring the hammer of justice down on them,” she wrote on social media.
In a Justice Department press release, both Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel portrayed the case as pushing back on what they described as a “weaponization” of government under the prior administration.
A judge set a preliminary hearing for the pair for Tuesday. Representatives for the defendants could not be immediately reached for comment.
Senate Judiciary Chair Charles E. Grassley, R-Iowa, praised the charges in a statement and said that ahead of the 2020 election, Floris and Benavides had falsely sought to portray as forwarding Russian disinformation an investigation he led into the Biden family.
“Today we’re seeing accountability efforts in action,” Grassley’s statement said.
The complaint comes days after the Trump administration faced criticism for executing a search warrant on the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., as the November midterms approach. A Justice Department manual states that investigators should not take steps “for the purpose” of affecting an election.

sources.text:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Two former FBI officials were charged Friday with lying to Congress about their involvement in investigating Hunter Biden’s laptop in the run-up to the 2020 presidential election, the latest in a series of splashy and politically charged actions the Justice Department has undertaken ahead of next month’s midterm contests.
Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former leaders of a since-disbanded task force set up to counter foreign election interference, appeared in federal court in Washington, where their lawyers pressed for a speedy hearing to contest allegations their clients lied to lawmakers by saying that they did not participate in FBI investigations of Biden.
The prosecution, a rare Department of Justice criminal case against a former employee, revisits a tangled and peculiar saga that roiled the final weeks of the 2020 race. It also comes amid a broader, backward-looking effort by FBI Director Kash Patel, who before taking over the nation’s premier law enforcement agency was a harsh critic of it, to scrutinize high-profile episodes from the bureau’s recent past that for years have animated President Donald Trump’s conservative base.
Floris’ attorneys called her “a patriot” and said she has “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years.”
“Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts,” her attorneys said in a statement. “It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.”
Attorneys for Benavides accused the government of bringing “baseless criminal charges against him in a transparently political complaint.”
“This is another sad day for the Department of Justice,” his lawyers said in an emailed statement. “But now we are in court, and the truth will come out: Brad Benavides is a true patriot who devoted his career to protecting this country and its people. These charges are a disgrace.”
A criminal complaint comes just before the midterms
The case was filed less than two weeks before the Nov. 3 elections via criminal complaint, which means prosecutors have not yet presented the allegations to a grand jury for an indictment. The Justice Department has repeatedly struggled in high-profile cases to convince grand juries in the nation’s capital to return indictments.
During the former FBI employees’ court appearance, both defense attorneys and the judge noted the unusual move to charge the case through a complaint, which is more often used by prosecutors when they have an urgent need to take people into custody because, for example, they present a danger or a risk of flight.
U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui remarked that it is “rare that we have charges this old coming in this nature,” and over the objections of prosecutors who pushed for more time, set a preliminary hearing for next Tuesday, citing what he said was the “sword of Damocles” hanging over the defendants’ heads.
The laptop discovery created turmoil in 2020 election
The revelation of the laptop’s existence in October 2020 injected a thorny storyline in the race between Trump, the Republican incumbent, and Biden’s father, Joe Biden, Trump’s Democratic challenger who went on to win the race.
The laptop were publicized by the New York Post, which said it had obtained from Trump ally Rudy Giuliani a hard drive of a computer dropped off by Hunter Biden at a Wilmington, Delaware, repair shop about a year earlier.
The criminal complaint aims to build on longstanding congressional Republican complaints about the FBI’s handling of the laptop, including allegations that the bureau was not forthcoming to the public that the materials on it — including emails that showed discussions of the younger Biden’s foreign business dealings — were authentic and not the product of Russian disinformation.
The curious circumstances of the laptop’s discovery raised concerns among Democrats and former intelligence officials about the possibility of Russian involvement, particularly at a time when the Trump administration’s own intelligence community had assessed that Moscow that Russia was attempting to interfere in Trump’s favor in the election and as Giuliani had traveled abroad looking for dirt on the Bidens. Dozens of former U.S. intelligence officials signed a letter saying that the laptop bore the “classic earmarks of an Russian information operation.”
But Trump’s then-director of national intelligence, John Ratcliffe, said in a letter to Congress that there was no proof foreign actors had anything to do with the laptop. The FBI under then-Director Chris Wray subsequently endorsed that position.
Hunter Biden was charged with, and convicted of, gun and tax offenses during his father’s administration. Joe Biden pardoned him in his final weeks in office.
The case shines a light on an FBI task force on foreign intelligence
The complaint alleges that in their capacity as leaders of the Foreign Influence Task Force, Floris and Benavides were deeply engaged in the investigations into Hunter Biden, and that Biden was a recurring subject at FITF meetings.
Yet, the complaint says, both downplayed their firsthand knowledge of the laptop or involvement in investigations during 2023 testimony to lawmakers who were doing their own Biden investigation.
It accuses Benavides of making a false statement by saying he learned through Wikipedia that the FBI was in possession of the laptop, and says Floris falsely claimed to have had no knowledge of Hunter Biden having been the subject of discussions at FITF.
“Lying to Congress by senior FBI officials strikes at the heart of our system. No one is above the law,” Patel said.
The case brings renewed attention to the work of the task force, which was established in the first Trump administration to police influence campaigns staged by Russia and other nations aimed at sowing discord, undermining democracy and spreading disinformation. The task force became a magnet of congressional Republican criticism in part because of the Hunter Biden investigation and was disbanded in February 2025 by then-Attorney General Pam Bondi.
The Justice Department has made other splashy moves
As FBI director, Patel has presided over widespread firings of agents who were involved in investigations of Trump or who are perceived as being against the Republican administration’s agenda.
He has also focused attention on years-old investigations like the Hunter Biden one that occurred before he became director and that have been the subject of grievances and complaints by Trump allies.
The Justice Department historically looks to avoid public and overt investigative acts in the direct lead-up to an election that involve candidates or that risk influencing a political outcome. But officials in the last two weeks have made a series of bold moves in cases with political undertones, including a search of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s house in an immigration fraud investigation and a corruption indictment unsealed Thursday against powerful Democratic Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas.
Omar and Lucas are both Trump critics. Omar, who’s from Minnesota, has called the search of her Washington home an “attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.” Lucas has said she won’t be intimidated or bullied by the federal government in its case against her and “will not back down.”

sources.text:
WASHINGTON – Two former FBI officials were charged Friday with lying to Congress about their involvement in investigating Hunter Biden’s laptop in the run-up to the 2020 presidential election, the latest in a series of splashy and politically charged actions the Justice Department has undertaken ahead of next month's midterm contests.
Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, former leaders of a since-disbanded task force set up to counter foreign election interference, appeared in federal court in Washington, where their lawyers pressed for a speedy hearing to contest allegations their clients lied to lawmakers by saying that they did not participate in FBI investigations of Biden.
Recommended Videos
The prosecution, a rare Department of Justice criminal case against a former employee, revisits a tangled and peculiar saga that roiled the final weeks of the 2020 race. It also comes amid a broader, backward-looking effort by FBI Director Kash Patel, who before taking over the nation’s premier law enforcement agency was a harsh critic of it, to scrutinize high-profile episodes from the bureau’s recent past that for years have animated President Donald Trump’s conservative base.
Floris’ attorneys called her “a patriot” and said she has “served our nation as a dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years.”
“Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts,” her attorneys said in a statement. “It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election.”
Attorneys for Benavides accused the government of bringing “baseless criminal charges against him in a transparently political complaint.”
“This is another sad day for the Department of Justice,” his lawyers said in an emailed statement. “But now we are in court, and the truth will come out: Brad Benavides is a true patriot who devoted his career to protecting this country and its people. These charges are a disgrace.”
A criminal complaint comes just before the midterms
The case was filed less than two weeks before the Nov. 3 elections via criminal complaint, which means prosecutors have not yet presented the allegations to a grand jury for an indictment. The Justice Department has repeatedly struggled in high-profile cases to convince grand juries in the nation’s capital to return indictments.
During the former FBI employees’ court appearance, both defense attorneys and the judge noted the unusual move to charge the case through a complaint, which is more often used by prosecutors when they have an urgent need to take people into custody because, for example, they present a danger or a risk of flight.
U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui remarked that it is “rare that we have charges this old coming in this nature," and over the objections of prosecutors who pushed for more time, set a preliminary hearing for next Tuesday, citing what he said was the “sword of Damocles” hanging over the defendants’ heads.
The laptop discovery created turmoil in 2020 election
The revelation of the laptop’s existence in October 2020 injected a thorny storyline in the race between Trump, the Republican incumbent, and Biden’s father, Joe Biden, Trump’s Democratic challenger who went on to win the race.
The laptop were publicized by the New York Post, which said it had obtained from Trump ally Rudy Giuliani a hard drive of a computer dropped off by Hunter Biden at a Wilmington, Delaware, repair shop about a year earlier.
The criminal complaint aims to build on longstanding congressional Republican complaints about the FBI’s handling of the laptop, including allegations that the bureau was not forthcoming to the public that the materials on it — including emails that showed discussions of the younger Biden’s foreign business dealings — were authentic and not the product of Russian disinformation.
The curious circumstances of the laptop’s discovery raised concerns among Democrats and former intelligence officials about the possibility of Russian involvement, particularly at a time when the Trump administration’s own intelligence community had assessed that Moscow that Russia was attempting to interfere in Trump’s favor in the election and as Giuliani had traveled abroad looking for dirt on the Bidens. Dozens of former U.S. intelligence officials signed a letter saying that the laptop bore the "classic earmarks of an Russian information operation.”
But Trump’s then-director of national intelligence, John Ratcliffe, said in a letter to Congress that there was no proof foreign actors had anything to do with the laptop. The FBI under then-Director Chris Wray subsequently endorsed that position.
Hunter Biden was charged with, and convicted of, gun and tax offenses during his father’s administration. Joe Biden pardoned him in his final weeks in office.
The case shines a light on an FBI task force on foreign intelligence
The complaint alleges that in their capacity as leaders of the Foreign Influence Task Force, Floris and Benavides were deeply engaged in the investigations into Hunter Biden, and that Biden was a recurring subject at FITF meetings.
Yet, the complaint says, both downplayed their firsthand knowledge of the laptop or involvement in investigations during 2023 testimony to lawmakers who were doing their own Biden investigation.
It accuses Benavides of making a false statement by saying he learned through Wikipedia that the FBI was in possession of the laptop, and says Floris falsely claimed to have had no knowledge of Hunter Biden having been the subject of discussions at FITF.
“Lying to Congress by senior FBI officials strikes at the heart of our system. No one is above the law,” Patel said.
The case brings renewed attention to the work of the task force, which was established in the first Trump administration to police influence campaigns staged by Russia and other nations aimed at sowing discord, undermining democracy and spreading disinformation. The task force became a magnet of congressional Republican criticism in part because of the Hunter Biden investigation and was disbanded in February 2025 by then-Attorney General Pam Bondi.
The Justice Department has made other splashy moves
As FBI director, Patel has presided over widespread firings of agents who were involved in investigations of Trump or who are perceived as being against the Republican administration's agenda.
He has also focused attention on years-old investigations like the Hunter Biden one that occurred before he became director and that have been the subject of grievances and complaints by Trump allies.
The Justice Department historically looks to avoid public and overt investigative acts in the direct lead-up to an election that involve candidates or that risk influencing a political outcome. But officials in the last two weeks have made a series of bold moves in cases with political undertones, including a search of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar’s house in an immigration fraud investigation and a corruption indictment unsealed Thursday against powerful Democratic Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas.
Omar and Lucas are both Trump critics. Omar, who's from Minnesota, has called the search of her Washington home an “attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement.” Lucas has said she won't be intimidated or bullied by the federal government in its case against her and “will not back down.”

sources.text:
Two former FBI officials are facing charges for allegedly lying to Congress as part of a probe that focused on whether FBI investigators sought to minimize allegations of Biden family corruption and evidence of Hunter Biden’s laptop, according to people briefed on the matter and court documents.
Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, both former top Washington-based intelligence specialists, are charged with one count of making a false statement. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui said in court on Friday the charges are related to “Hunter Biden’s laptop and allegations around that.”
The charges, which come less than two weeks before Election Day, relate to statements Floris and Benavides made to the House Judiciary Committee in 2023 as Republicans questioned an FBI election interference task force’s involvement in the Hunter Biden investigations.
A charging document unsealed in DC’s federal district court Friday accuses the pair of “concealing [the task force’s] engagement with and communications about the Hunter Biden investigations and impeding the congressional investigation.”
DC US Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced the charges in a social media post on Friday, saying the alleged false statements were “about their roles on the Foreign Influence Task Force during the 2020 election.”
Pirro added that “when senior FBI agents lie to Congress believing they are above the law, it’s time to bring the hammer of justice down on them.”
FBI Director Kash Patel said Friday that the charges are the result of an investigation into the since-dissolved task force.
He also says Floris is “on record privately claiming” to be running a shadow government.
“Floris led the FITF as a Deputy Assistant Director from mid-2019 through mid-2022. Benavides was the FITF Section Chief from mid-2019 through the 2020 election,” he said on X. “Both testified that the FITF was not involved in the Hunter Biden investigations. Documentary evidence, contemporaneous communications, and witness accounts contradict their testimony.”
“Lying to Congress by senior FBI officials strikes at the heart of our system. No one is above the law,” he continued.
According to Pirro and the criminal complaint, Benavides told Congress he learned about the investigation into Hunter Biden’s laptop from Wikipedia.
Republicans have repeatedly criticized the FBI for its early handling of investigations into Hunter Biden as part of long-running theories about corruption in the Biden family and so-called “deep state” right-wing narratives about the federal government.
The two defendants made their first appearance in the federal district court in DC Friday morning. They will not be detained as they await trial.
A hearing for the former FBI officials is scheduled for Tuesday morning.
Faruqui noted that both agents have “sparkling backgrounds” and told prosecutors the “alleged context happened years ago.” The judge noted the prosecutors should be ready to move forward with the case given that they “brought this serious charge against two decorated agents.”
He also noted the charge was “rare” and made note that it was charged by complaint from prosecutors, and not approved by a grand jury.
Faruqui also said on the bench Friday the charges were “straightforward” and that the agents, with otherwise sterling records, are now charged in federal court, which will “follow them for the rest of their lives.”
Defense attorneys for Floris, in a statement following her appearance in court, said she is being falsely accused “on the say-so of politicians” and “is a patriot.”
“It’s no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election,” the lawyers said in their statement.
“The government’s reasons for charging Nikki are as transparent as they are unjust: to push a false narrative for a shot at political politics.”
The dismantled task force
The FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force was established in Trump’s first administration to track and combat foreign influence campaigns aimed at US elections after FBI agents were caught off-guard by the scale of Russia’s 2016 influence operations.
The task force, which consisted of about 30 FBI personnel, passed intelligence about what foreign spies were doing on social media platform such as Facebook and Twitter. The platforms could choose whether to suspend the accounts or not.
In February 2025, then-Attorney General Pam Bondi dissolved FITF, citing the need to “free resources to address more pressing priorities, and end risks of further weaponization and abuses of prosecutorial discretion.”
Former US officials who worked to defend elections from foreign influence reacted with disgust to what they saw as politically motivated charges against Floris and Benavides.
“I’m amazed that the administration is focused on this, fighting imaginary adversaries of the past and perceived political grievances,” one former US official told CNN. “Nikki and Brad are dedicated professionals and were key to combating the efforts of Russia, China, and Iran.”
Trump and Republicans have accused the Bidens of corruption, especially after IRS whistleblowers claimed the FBI had slow-walked an investigation into Hunter Biden while his father was in office.
A special counsel thoroughly investigated the Republicans’ allegations against Hunter Biden and didn’t recommend any additional charges past the gun and tax charges. A separate government informant was charged by that special counsel, David Weiss, for providing false information alleging bribery in the Biden family.
Biden’s son Hunter was ultimately convicted of federal tax and gun charges, then pardoned by his father in late 2024 after Trump won the presidential election.
This story was updated with additional reporting from court.
CNN’s Caitlin McCormack contributed to this report.
