sources.news_title: JUST IN: Two Former Top FBI Officials Taken Into Custody
sources.text:
Two former senior FBI officials are now facing federal charges over what prosecutors say they told Congress about the bureau’s Hunter Biden investigations.
Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides surrendered Friday on arrest warrants issued after a criminal complaint charged each of them with making false statements to Congress.
The two defendants once held leadership positions inside the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force, the unit created to defend the 2020 election from foreign interference.
Now federal prosecutors say both officials concealed how deeply that task force had been involved in matters connected to Hunter Biden.
U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced the arrests Friday morning:
This morning, two former senior FBI officials, Nikki Floris, 46, and Bradley Benavides, 56, surrendered on arrest warrants after being charged with lying to Congress about their roles on the Foreign Influence Task Force during the 2020 election. Floris and Benavides allegedly…
— US Attorney Pirro (@USAttyPirro) October 23, 2026
According to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Columbia, Floris, 46, of Alexandria, Virginia, led the Foreign Influence Task Force as a deputy assistant director from mid-2019 through mid-2022. The unit coordinated the bureau’s response to suspected foreign efforts to influence American elections.
Benavides, 56, of Aiken, South Carolina, served as the task force’s section chief from mid-2019 through the 2020 election. Prosecutors say both officials were involved in briefings and communications touching the Hunter Biden matters.
That timing is central to the case.
The Justice Department says the task force participated in several FBI investigations involving Hunter Biden before the 2020 election. In 2023, the House Judiciary Committee interviewed Floris and Benavides about that work and warned each of them that lying to Congress was a crime.
Prosecutors allege Floris told lawmakers she had not been involved in discussions about Hunter Biden while leading the task force.
Benavides allegedly testified that he learned the FBI possessed Hunter Biden’s laptop only after reading a Wikipedia article in 2023.
The criminal complaint tells a very different story.
According to prosecutors, documentary evidence, contemporaneous communications and witness accounts show Floris routinely discussed the bureau’s Hunter Biden investigations for more than a year. The government also alleges Benavides discussed the laptop with other FBI officials before the 2020 election.
The department says each defendant is charged with one count of making false statements in a matter within the jurisdiction of the legislative branch, an alleged violation of 18 U.S.C. § 1001(a)(2).
Its announcement emphasizes that the task force led the FBI’s efforts to protect the election from foreign malign influence while also participating in several Hunter Biden investigations.
That combination is why the 2023 testimony matters so much. Congress was not asking two peripheral employees what they had heard through office gossip.
Lawmakers were questioning the former leaders of the unit that prosecutors now say took part in the very matters they denied knowing about.
FBI Director Kash Patel said the arrests grew out of an ongoing investigation into the now-dissolved task force:
Two former senior FBI officials, Nikki Cole Floris and Bradley Benavides, were taken into custody today on charges of allegedly lying to Congress about their involvement in the FBI’s investigations into Hunter Biden.
The charges stem from an ongoing investigation into the…
— FBI Director Kash Patel (@FBIDirectorKash) October 23, 2026
Each defendant is charged with one count of making false statements in a matter within the jurisdiction of the legislative branch, an alleged violation of 18 U.S.C. § 1001(a)(2).
That statute makes the alleged lie—not the underlying Hunter Biden investigation—the immediate criminal issue before the court.
The complaint does not establish that either defendant manipulated the 2020 election, suppressed the laptop story or improperly influenced the underlying investigations. Prosecutors will have to prove the charged false statements with admissible evidence.
The charging papers do, however, revive one of the most bitter disputes from the final weeks of the 2020 campaign: what the FBI knew about Hunter Biden’s laptop, how the bureau treated the material and what senior officials later told congressional investigators.
The Associated Press reported that both defendants appeared in federal court in Washington after surrendering. Their attorneys pressed for a fast opportunity to challenge the government’s evidence.
The case arrived through a criminal complaint rather than a grand-jury indictment, a procedural choice that drew attention inside the courtroom because the alleged statements date back to 2023.
U.S. Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui set a preliminary hearing for Tuesday after the defense objected to a longer delay. At that hearing, prosecutors are expected to face an early test of whether the complaint establishes probable cause.
The judge reportedly described the unresolved accusation as a “sword of Damocles” hanging over the defendants and noted the rarity of old allegations arriving in this form. Prosecutors asked for more time, but the court chose a faster timetable, giving the defense an unusually quick chance to test the government’s theory.
Floris’ attorneys flatly deny the accusation.
They described her as a patriot who served in FBI intelligence for nearly two decades and accused the Justice Department of filing a politically motivated case shortly before the midterm election. Their response makes clear that the government should expect an aggressive fight over the evidence, the timing and the meaning of her congressional testimony.
CBS News reviewed the complaint and reported that it centers on the officials’ alleged awareness of and involvement in the Hunter Biden investigations. The filing cites witness accounts and records from 2019 through 2021 that prosecutors say contradict the defendants’ later testimony.
The complaint describes a counterintelligence operation called “Round River,” which allegedly collected derogatory informant reporting involving Hunter Biden so the material could be assessed for possible Russian disinformation. Prosecutors say task-force leaders participated in classified briefings for agents and prosecutors working on the Hunter Biden matters.
It also cites a congressional staff member who attended both interviews and later told investigators that the officials’ testimony appeared materially untrue. An FBI employee separately told investigators that he had spoken with Benavides about the laptop and discussed reviewing its contents.
One allegation is already drawing enormous political attention.
Patel said one of the former officials had privately claimed to be “running a shadow government” during the 2020 election. The Justice Department’s announcement did not fully explain the context of that statement, and the remark itself is not the false statement charged in the complaint.
House Judiciary Committee Republicans identified Floris in their reaction:
Nikki Floris admitted she was running a “shadow government.”
Today the real government caught her. pic.twitter.com/ExjzMeI6bk
— House Judiciary GOP 🇺🇸🇺🇸🇺🇸 (@JudiciaryGOP) October 23, 2026
That line will dominate the political conversation.
But the courtroom battle will turn on something narrower and more concrete: the exact questions Congress asked, the exact answers Floris and Benavides gave, what they knew at the time and whether prosecutors can prove beyond a reasonable doubt that either answer was knowingly false.
The documents and witness testimony described by the government may be substantial. They have not yet been tested through cross-examination.
Both defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.
The next major moment comes Tuesday, when the Justice Department will have to begin moving this case from a dramatic announcement toward evidence that can survive in court.

Updated October 23, 2026 at 11:50 AM PDT
The Justice Department has charged two former FBI employees with making false statements to Congress in connection with the bureau's investigations into Hunter Biden and his laptop ahead of the 2020 presidential election.
Bradley Benavides and Nikki Floris each face a single criminal count stemming from testimony before lawmakers in 2023. The pair, who held senior positions on the FBI's now defunct Foreign Influence Task Force, both turned themselves in and made their initial court appearance Friday morning in Washington, D.C.
The new prosecution is the latest politically fraught case to be brought by the Justice Department since President Trump returned to the White House. It dredges back up the bizarre saga surrounding former President Joe Biden's son, Hunter Biden, and his various legal troubles that featured throughout the 2020 presidential campaign.
Hunter Biden's laptop was the subject of intense scrutiny after The New York Post reported weeks before the 2020 presidential election that the device was abandoned at a Delaware repair shop in 2019, and then obtained by President Trump's former personal lawyer Rudy Giuliani.
Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden. Hunter Biden was convicted of federal gun charges and later pleaded guilty to separate tax offenses. (Joe Biden signed a full and unconditional pardon for his son in December 2024.)
In a statement on X, the U.S. attorney for Washington, D.C., Jeanine Pirro, said Floris and Benavides "allegedly lied to Congress about their roles in the FBI's Hunter Biden investigations, with one claiming they only learned about it from Wikipedia — despite evidence showing their involvement in helping shape the public narrative about Hunter Biden's laptop right before the election."
Prosecutors charged Benavides and Floris by criminal complaint, which means prosecutors have yet to secure an indictment from a grand jury. Under the second Trump administration, grand juries in the nation's capital and other cities have refused on several occasions to return indictments in high-profile, politically charged cases.
At a court hearing Friday morning, Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui noted that both of the defendants have "sparkling backgrounds" in federal law enforcement and were longtime dedicated public servants. He also noted that charging them by criminal complaint for conduct that is "quite old" is unusual.
Court hearing planned next week
Benavides, 56, and Floris, 46, are due back in court for a preliminary hearing on Tuesday.
In a statement, Floris' attorneys called her a "patriot" who served as "dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years."
"Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts. It's no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election," they added.
The Post reported Hunter Biden's laptop showed wrongdoing by then-Democratic nominee Joe Biden, who subsequently won the election. Some of the data on the laptop was later ascertained to belong to Hunter Biden. House Republicans subsequently launched an impeachment inquiry into President Biden, focusing on Hunter Biden's business dealings at the time his father was vice president. But no evidence has ever been presented that Joe Biden financially gained from his son's business activities.
The complaint alleges that Benavides and Floris both had real-time knowledge of the Hunter Biden investigations, including into his laptop, in their top posts on the Foreign Influence Task Force.
But in interviews with the House Judiciary Committee in 2023, both of them allegedly lied about their knowledge and involvement in those investigations.
Those purported false statements were material to the committee's investigation, the complaint says, because they allowed both Benavides and Floris to "escape" further questioning about Hunter Biden, which hindered the panel's investigation.
